fixes.why: The summary says Lutheran and Reformed readers hold this 'under names of their own', and then gives compatibilism, which the terms note itself calls a philosophers' term used by many Lutheran and Reformed readers. Lutheran readers do not use compatibilism as their own name, and Reformed readers do use it. The sentence claims more uniformity than the terms note allows.
fixes.fix: Summary, replace 'Lutheran and Reformed readers hold this under names of their own (the bondage of the will, and compatibilism, the view that God's ordering of events and a person's own choosing are both true), with a shared concern' with 'Lutheran and Reformed readers hold this, and name it in their own terms: the bondage of the will is shared, and among Reformed readers compatibilism, the view that God's ordering of events and a person's own choosing are both true, is used as well; both hold a shared concern'. Terms note for compatibilism, replace 'used by many Lutheran and Reformed readers' with 'used by many Reformed readers, and by some Lutheran ones'.

fixes.why: The answer restates Romans 8:7 as 'a will weakened by sin', but the verse says the mind 'does not submit to God's law, nor can it do so'. Weakened softens the word 'cannot', which is the point the second reading takes from the same verse. The first reading's holders would say the wound is real and the loss is not, and the card should say that in their terms.
fixes.fix: Replace 'They take Romans 8:7 and John 8:34 to describe a will weakened by sin and inclined toward it, which grace heals.' with 'They take Romans 8:7 and John 8:34 to describe a will wounded by sin and inclined toward it, which grace heals; they read Romans 8:7's "nor can it do so" as the wound of the will and not its loss.'

fixes.why: Reading 3 is the reading whose holders most often cite the open offer to whoever calls or believes, and no verse of that kind is on the card. Romans 10:13 is the verse these holders take first for the universal call, and the card has none. To keep the count at eight each, the fix swaps out Hebrews 3:15, which is the weaker fit for this reading and overlaps with Acts 17:30.
fixes.fix: Add {"ref": "Romans 10:13", "quote": "Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.", "note": "The call to whoever calls, in the words the early church took from Joel."} and remove the Hebrews 3:15 entry. Berean text of Romans 10:13 is 'for, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.”', and the quote above is the verse's clause. Alternative for a reviewer to weigh: John 3:16, 'that everyone who believes in Him shall not perish but have eternal life', which would be a ninth entry unless another is dropped.

fixes.where: reading 2 answers and passage note for Ezekiel 36:27
fixes.why: Ezekiel 36:27 is spoken to Israel as a promise of restoration to the nation, and the card gives it only a neutral note ('God's promise to cause the walking he commands'). The Christian reading of the Spirit's work in believers is the holders' reading, and rule 8 asks that the note say so. The rabbi would otherwise see a Hebrew prophecy about Israel presented as the settled answer to an individual question.
fixes.fix: Replace the note for Ezekiel 36:27 with 'Spoken to Israel as a promise of restoration; these holders read it of the Spirit's work in believers, and the verse's first hearers are the people of Israel.'

summary: All 29 quotes match the Berean exactly, and each reading's held_by, its verses and the agreed block are fair on the whole. Four fixes make it ship: the Lutheran and Reformed wording on compatibilism, the Romans 8:7 'weakened' gloss in reading 1, a missing universal-call verse in reading 3, and the Ezekiel 36:27 framing for the rabbi's seat.
